quotes.text: You assumed automation meant reliability, when in reality, automation just amplifies your errors faster and with more confidence than any intern ever could.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core warning about unvalidated automation.

quotes.text: Every automated decision should trace back to verified input. Without that checkpoint, you're not automating, you're accelerating mistakes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear governance principle for AI-driven workflows.

quotes.text: Automation was never supposed to remove humans from the loop. It was supposed to remove their laziness from the loop.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable reframing of why human validation belongs in automation.

quotes.text: Think of it like physical security. The AI prompt is the surveillance camera it observes and analyzes. The RFI is the locked door. It refuses entry until you flash verified credentials.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Analogy that explains how AI validation and RFI complement each other.

quotes.text: Here's the thing most people eventually realize. Reliability isn't about smarter AI. It's about stricter governance.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise summary of the episode's thesis.

takeaways: AI flows fail mostly because they trust incomplete or wrong human input, not because the AI misbehaves.
The request for information action in Copilot Studio agent flows pauses execution and collects missing data through an Outlook actionable message, leaving a traceable record of who confirmed what.
Pairing AI prompt validation with RFI creates a governance loop in which AI detects gaps and humans confirm reality before data reaches Dataverse.
hook: Your Copilot Studio flow did exactly what you told it to, with bad data. This episode is for makers, Power Platform admins and compliance teams who need automations they can defend in an audit. Learn how the request for information action adds a human firewall that stops null values, phantom records and false approvals.
